rules.title: Interactive controls have keyboard semantics
rules.applicability: Focusable actions and navigation.
exceptions: Use links for navigation and buttons for actions; specialized widgets follow their own keyboard model.
rules.repair: Use native semantics; test activation, names and disabled states.

rules.title: Retain edits and report persistence truthfully
rules.applicability: Forms that save through an asynchronous service.
exceptions: A queued write may say queued, never persisted; explicit discard may clear data.
rules.repair: Keep draft and committed data separate; reject stale responses; retry rejected writes without clearing input.

rules.title: Errors identify and link to the relevant field
rules.applicability: Detected input errors.
exceptions: A summary is a contextual implementation, not itself a WCAG requirement; sensitive error detail may be withheld.
rules.repair: Use one error model for inline messages and summary links; preserve valid description IDs and focus the linked control.

rules.title: Choose validation and unsaved-work policy deliberately
rules.applicability: Editing and attempted cancellation or navigation.
exceptions: Do not block navigation for pristine forms; autosave requires its own truthful operation model.
rules.repair: Document submit/blur timing and connect requestLeave to cancel, router Back and navigation; explain browser unload limits.
verification: manual: exercise cancel, Back, reload and route change with unsaved data

rules.title: Distinguish collection states and retain identity
rules.applicability: Asynchronously loaded collections.
exceptions: First-use empty and no-results apply only when the application knows the distinction; offline/cache may add states.
rules.repair: Render loading, refreshing, empty, filtered empty and failure accurately; use stable keys and an explicit selection policy.

rules.title: Confirm intent separately from operation completion
rules.applicability: Actions with significant consequences.
exceptions: Direct actions are suitable when real recovery exists; confirmation is not universal.
rules.repair: Name target and consequence; delay success until execute resolves; wire real undo or appropriate review, and logical focus.

rules.title: Allow correction and preserve a truthful receipt
rules.applicability: Processes with a review step before final commitment.
exceptions: Not every short form needs a separate review screen; redundant-entry and error-prevention criteria have scoped exceptions.
rules.repair: Retain applicable answers through correction and failed submission; show a service-issued receipt and a durable destination.

rules.title: Status is perceivable without moving focus unnecessarily
rules.applicability: Status messages that do not receive focus.
exceptions: Urgent errors may use alerts; avoid announcing every keystroke or repeated decorative status.
rules.repair: Use an appropriate live region and concise meaningful messages; test feedback with assistive technology.

rules.title: Height has an equivalent non-depth signal
rules.applicability: All meaning carried by elevation.
exceptions: Decorative depth carries no required semantic meaning.
rules.repair: Pair depth with text, state or border and inspect forced colors/reduced motion.
verification: manual: forced colors, reduced motion, zoom and RTL review

rules.title: Hold-to-confirm remains a scoped hypothesis
rules.applicability: Considering hold gestures for consequential actions.
exceptions: Never require a hold as the sole accessible way to complete a task.
rules.repair: Choose review or real recovery from task consequences; evaluate hold benefits with representative users.

rules.title: Installed guidance and setup versions agree
rules.applicability: Projects using the explicit CLI adapter.
exceptions: Projects may read local guidance directly without configuring an agent.
rules.repair: Reinstall/build the matching package and rerun altitude init for configured clients.

rules.title: One primary action per view
rules.applicability: Any view: a page, and each Dialog, Sheet and Popover. Independent parts (cards on a dashboard) can be scoped with PrimaryScope.
exceptions: A dashboard of independent cards, each with its own task, wrapped in PrimaryScope.
rules.repair: Keep one Button variant="primary" per view (PageHeader's primary slot on a page); make the rest secondary or ghost, or put them in an overflow menu.

rules.title: Persistent states don't rise
rules.applicability: States that feel important but persist: unread, invited (awaiting someone else), recommended or most popular, current plan or item, locked behind a plan, an app-wide mode, proposed by an agent, streaming text.
exceptions: A state that is live right now (a write in flight, something in a hand, an action being asked for) uses its own signal from Elevation.md.
rules.repair: Say the state in words, a plate, a dot, weight or an ARIA state, and keep the thing at its own level: unread is a dot and weight 600; invited is a plate, not pending; recommended is a plate with only its CTA at level 2; current is the word and aria-current; locked stays live and opens the upgrade; a mode is a strip and a viewport border; an agent's proposal is raised, asking; streaming text stays on the ground and settles once. See Elevation.md, "States that don't rise".
verification: manual:review the screen against Elevation.md, "States that don't rise"

rules.title: Each settings section applies now or saves together, and destructive actions sit in a final danger zone
rules.applicability: Settings pages that combine standalone preferences, records saved together and destructive actions.
exceptions: A page with only one mode needs only that mode; a single destructive action outside settings follows the consequential-action contract alone.
rules.repair: Give each section one mode: apply-now controls report their own write (pending, committed, failed with the control restored); fields that form one record join one draft saved once. Move delete, transfer and similar actions to a final section titled Danger zone, at the same height as the others, each named by its outcome with its consequence in words.

rules.title: Invitations are settled records, and guards are said where the action would be
rules.applicability: Member lists with invitations, roles and removal.
exceptions: Products without invitations or roles apply only the guard requirement.
rules.repair: Draw an invitation awaiting acceptance on the ground with an Invited plate, its role and sent date; hover only while sending. Replace an action a person may not take (removing the last owner, demoting yourself out of the last admin role) with the reason in words, and enforce the same guard on the server.

rules.title: Usage is a reading, a plan change is reviewed with its cost, and a downgrade lists what's lost
rules.applicability: Billing pages with usage limits and plan changes.
exceptions: Prices and proration are the billing service's; the interface shows what the service quotes and never computes a charge itself.
rules.repair: Draw each quota as a Meter with its state in words, never Progress; mark the rest of the cycle as projected; review a plan change with the quoted proration as a sentence before confirming, and claim it only after the service confirms; list what a downgrade removes and name its button by the outcome.

rules.title: Auth copy reveals nothing, fields carry autocomplete tokens, and nothing is submitted for the person
rules.applicability: Sign-in, sign-up, verification, two-factor and reset screens.
exceptions: Products that delegate authentication to a hosted provider apply this to the parts they render.
rules.repair: Use responses that hold whether or not the account exists; state rate limits with the wait; give every field its autocomplete token and allow paste; keep Verify and Sign in as buttons the person presses; keep the email across steps; offer a path that isn't a cognitive test.

rules.title: Audit entries are flush sentences that expand to their change, and export is a job
rules.applicability: Audit logs and activity feeds.
exceptions: Entries that link somewhere may lift when pointed at; nothing else does.
rules.repair: Render each entry as a flush row that reads as one sentence with its actor, exact time and origin; expand it to the before and after; keep the workspace log and a record's feed apart; run export as a task with progress, then offer the download and log the export.

rules.title: Mapping shows what's left, invalid cells sink with their problem, and the import ends with a receipt
rules.applicability: File imports with mapping and row validation.
exceptions: Imports with a fixed format skip mapping; the fix, review and receipt still apply.
rules.repair: Give each source column a Select that fills when mapped and list unmapped required fields in words; show invalid cells as trenches with their problem in the cell's description and announce the count as it changes; review in one sentence of consequences; run the import as a job with progress, cancellation where supported, and a receipt of imported, skipped and failed rows.

rules.title: Nothing is saved until the server says so, queued work is visible, and no edit is dropped silently
rules.applicability: Autosaving, optimistic and local-first work, and expiring sessions.
exceptions: Automatic merges need no prompt; only conflicts the merge strategy can't resolve ask the person.
rules.repair: Keep each change pending until acknowledged and say Saved only when the queue is empty; show offline changes as waiting with a count; show unresolved conflicts with both versions, the other in its author's presence colour and name, and say where the version not kept went; warn before a session expires, offer to extend it and keep drafts across re-authentication.

rules.title: A secret is shown once behind an acknowledgement, listed masked, and its roll or revocation says what happens
rules.applicability: API keys, signing secrets and integrations.
exceptions: Products that deliberately allow revealing a stored secret offer it on demand, masked by default.
rules.repair: Show a new secret in full once, in a dialog that closes only after the person confirms they saved it; list secrets masked with their last use; say a roll's overlap window before and after; name what breaks before revoking or disconnecting; show a retry as a pending write with its attempt.

rules.title: Each agent state is one reading, approval scales with consequence, and changes keep their provenance
rules.applicability: Embedded agents that act on someone's behalf.
exceptions: Steps with a real undo may run without approval; the application decides which.
rules.repair: Draw a proposal as raised and asking, never pending; hover only once approved and executing; land on the runtime's confirmation; sink failures with Retry; require a Confirmation for external or irreversible steps and a hold or stationary dialog for the most severe; put an AI label and the approver on every change; announce step changes politely and never token by token.

rules.title: Setup tasks are stamped when they happen, progress is a reading, and tours wait to be asked
rules.applicability: First-run setup, empty states, tours and release notes.
exceptions: A tour may be offered once after a change to existing UI; it still never starts on every visit.
rules.repair: Stamp a setup task done from the application event, not a click on the item; show progress as a Meter; open each empty region with its one action; offer tours rather than starting them, keep them short and never dim the page; count only unseen changes; make every onboarding surface dismissible and re-findable from Help.

rules.title: A screen's frame is chosen from its task, with one lead and one primary action named first
rules.applicability: Any new screen or app: its frame, what leads and where the primary action sits.
exceptions: An existing product keeps its navigation frame; the view inside it still names its task and lead.
rules.repair: Write down the task, the one thing that leads, the one primary action and what comes next; choose the frame from the task (records, list and detail, focused editor, guided flow, decision, report) instead of the sidebar-and-cards default; put the lead first after the title and make it the largest region; then check that every stated choice is visible on the screen.

rules.title: A conversation never loses the person's words, completes only when the stream does, and says each failure in words
rules.applicability: Conversations with an assistant: chat, copilots, agent conversations.
exceptions: What persists across reloads, and for how long, is the application's decision.
rules.repair: Guard against double submits; ignore events from a superseded turn; keep the partial answer on Stop as "Stopped"; settle an answer only when the stream says it's complete and show an unfinished one after a reload as "Interrupted" with Retry; keep the message when sending fails; say offline, rate limited (with when), context full, refused and outage as distinct states with what to do; announce each answer once, never token by token.

rules.title: Links, buttons, fields, images and headings name what they are
rules.applicability: Every link, button (including icon-only ones), form field, informative image and heading in a view.
exceptions: A decorative image takes an empty alt and needs no name.
Repeated links in a list ("Edit") are acceptable when their accessible name adds the object ("Edit invoice 1043").
rules.repair: Name links by destination, not "Learn more" or "Click here"; name buttons by verb and object; give every field a visible label, never a placeholder alone; describe what an image shows or mark it decorative; make each heading describe its section, with one h1 per view, no skipped levels, and header, nav and main landmarks.
verification: manual: read the view's links, buttons and headings out of context with a screen reader's rotor or list

rules.title: Emphasis serves the person's task: no false urgency, hidden terms, pre-selected costs or traps
rules.applicability: Sign-up, subscription, upgrade, checkout, discount, newsletter, consent and cancellation flows, and any overlay that asks for a decision.
exceptions: A real deadline (a trial end, a session timeout) is stated with its time.
A recommendation is shown as a plate or a sentence, not with extra height or size.
rules.repair: Remove countdowns and scarcity claims with no real limit; in offers the product makes, make declining at least a secondary button, as findable as accepting, named plainly and never shaming; pre-select nothing that costs money, shares data or subscribes; let every overlay close with Escape, and give anything that blocks the page a visible close or Cancel; put prices and terms beside their action at body size; let people leave in no more steps than they joined; show only real reviews and counts, saying how they were chosen.
verification: manual: review revenue, retention and data-collection flows for each deceptive pattern type, comparing the steps to accept and to decline

rules.title: Colours come from the tokens, not literals
rules.applicability: Colour values in an application's CSS declarations, inline styles and colour props.
exceptions: Defining tokens: a custom property (--brand: #…) or a custom scheme's token entries.
AltitudeProvider accent, which takes a colour literal by design.
A colour that must be literal (a third-party brand mark), marked altitude-ignore: ALT-TOKEN-001 with the reason.
rules.repair: Use a token (var(--ink-muted), var(--accent), var(--surface-raised)). A brand colour goes to AltitudeProvider accent; a full palette to a custom scheme.

rules.title: Altitude's stylesheet is imported
rules.applicability: An application that imports components from altitude-design.
exceptions: A page that loads the stylesheet with a <link> outside the scanned sources.
rules.repair: Import altitude-design/altitude.css (or altitude.no-fonts.css) once at the app's entry.

rules.title: The app is wrapped in AltitudeProvider
rules.applicability: An application that imports components from altitude-design.
exceptions: Several providers on purpose (separate React roots, previews): reported for review, not as an error.
rules.repair: Render one AltitudeProvider around the whole app; it sets the scheme and hosts dialogs and toasts.

rules.title: No pie or donut charts
rules.applicability: Charts drawn with recharts, react-chartjs-2, Chart.js, ECharts or Nivo in an Altitude application.
rules.repair: Show a part of a whole as a stacked BarChart or a segmented Meter: angle and area are read less accurately than length.

rules.title: One axis per plot
rules.applicability: Recharts charts in an Altitude application. Altitude's own charts have one value axis by construction.
exceptions: A second YAxis that is hidden and carries no series is still reported: remove it.
rules.repair: Two measures of different scale are two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base: two scales on one plot invite a correlation the data never made.

rules.title: Bars stand on zero
rules.applicability: Recharts bar charts (a YAxis domain starting at dataMin, auto or a positive number) and Altitude's ChartContainer holding a BarChart with a literal yDomain that leaves out zero.
exceptions: Values where zero isn't meaningful belong in a DotPlot or a line, not bars.
rules.repair: Keep zero on a bar chart's value axis: a bar that starts above zero misstates its length.

rules.title: Marks are flat ink
rules.applicability: Recharts marks (a url(#…) gradient fill, a filter, a radius rounding a bar's foot) and Altitude's chart types (a filter or style filter).
rules.repair: Draw marks as flat ink in a series colour: no gradient, shadow, glow or sheen, and round only a bar's data end. Depth costs accuracy, and a sheen says press it.

rules.title: Colour does one job
rules.applicability: A ChartConfig series given accent, a presence hue or a status colour; a Recharts mark coloured var(--accent…) or var(--presence-…); shadcn/ui's --chart-N custom properties set to anything but var(--data-1…6|other).
exceptions: A series that means good or bad may take a status colour in a chart Altitude doesn't draw, with an icon and a word; mark it with altitude-ignore and the reason.
rules.repair: Colour series from the data palette (data-1 to data-6, data-other): the accent, presence and status hues already mean something else.

rules.title: Every chart has a name
rules.applicability: Altitude's ChartContainer without title, aria-label or aria-labelledby; a Recharts chart without a title, aria-label or aria-labelledby, or with accessibilityLayer={false}.
exceptions: Props spread onto the chart ({...props}) aren't read and aren't reported.
A Recharts chart named by a wrapping role="img" element with aria-label: mark it with altitude-ignore and the reason.
rules.repair: Name the chart (title, or aria-labelledby pointing at the heading that names it) and keep Recharts' accessibilityLayer on.

rules.title: No decorative entrances
rules.applicability: Recharts marks, which animate in on first render unless isAnimationActive is false: a mark without it, with it true, or with a positive animationBegin stagger.
exceptions: isAnimationActive set from an expression (a reduced-motion or first-render hook) isn't reported.
rules.repair: Set isAnimationActive={false}, or a value that's false on first render and under reduced motion: a chart is simply there, and nothing grows from the baseline for decoration.

rules.title: A chart that leads a report says one thing first
rules.applicability: The first Altitude ChartContainer in a file that renders <main>, with no takeaway.
exceptions: A row of equal dashboard cards can do without a takeaway; whether this chart leads a report is a judgment.
rules.repair: Give the chart that leads a report a takeaway: the one thing it says, written from the data shown, as a trend or a comparison.

rules.title: Importance is emphasis
rules.applicability: An Altitude ChartContainer whose inline config has three or more series, with no focus on its chart type and no takeaway.
exceptions: A chart whose series matter equally (a comparison with no lead) needs neither; a config held in a variable isn't counted.
rules.repair: Say which series matters: focus on the chart type keeps its colour and sets the rest in data-context, and a takeaway names it.

rules.title: Buttons name their outcome, never OK or Submit
rules.applicability: Button labels written as literal text.
exceptions: A label computed at runtime is not checked.
rules.repair: Start with a verb and name the outcome: "Save changes", "Send invite".

rules.title: One primary action per view
rules.applicability: Files with more than one primary Button; they may or may not be on screen together.
exceptions: Primary buttons in different views, steps or dialogs that are never shown together.
rules.repair: Keep one primary, the action the task leads to; make the others secondary or ghost.

rules.title: Controls keep Altitude's elevation
rules.applicability: Shadow or transform overrides on Input, Textarea, Select, Combobox, Button, Switch or Checkbox.
exceptions: An override that doesn't change the control's apparent height.
rules.repair: Remove the override: a control's height says whether you press it or fill it. Use its variant and size props.

rules.title: Choose record detail from the task and preserve source correspondence
rules.applicability: A record opens in anchored, expanded, reserved, inspector, sheet or route detail.
exceptions: Not every detail needs an overlay, a current-item marker on an unavailable modal background, or a durable URL.
Existing navigation frames can remain; the detail task still determines its presentation and return policy.
rules.repair: Record the detail task, duration, information size, comparison, viewport, background interaction and history needs; use the screen-layout chooser. Bind to a stable ID, identify the source visibly, distinguish reserved space from opening-induced layout shifts, and define keyboard entry/close and a named fallback if the source disappears. Preserve negative preference evidence and test long/narrow boundaries.
verification: manual: review the actual detail task, source changes/removal, long content, narrow/zoom and assistive-technology behaviour
